text: Applying to a PhD is a team sport that most students play alone.
Offer room gives one student a team, in the chat app she already uses: six AI agents, each starting from a different place. They agree, add, or push back with evidence. She decides.
It's built with Switch. One template creates six Claude Code agents on this laptop, and five Discord rooms. They hand work to each other by mention, like teammates.
Meet two applicants. Both are fictional, and I type their side of the chat.
Priya, in Tamil Nadu, wants AI that understands her grandmother's Tamil. Her family can afford two applications.
Maya, in El Paso, is the first in her family to go to college, with three hundred dollars saved.
Priya asks the team: which two of Washington, Maryland and Cornell? Scout answers from the programs' own pages: Washington and Cornell, for cost and deadlines.
Mentor disagrees, with papers: Maryland has the clearest lab. Critic checks both against her record, and closes the round: where they agree, where they split, and what only she can decide.
She pushes back. Mentor runs a topic search, finds a Cornell professor it had missed, and says so first: I was wrong. Critic withdraws two claims, and the team agrees.

Getting in is only the start. In the mentor room, she asks where each lab's students went. Mentor reads the professor's own students page: industry research, no faculty jobs. And it flags what it couldn't confirm.
At the funding desk, both students ask the same question.
Maya can apply everywhere. Every school has a waiver she qualifies for, quoted line by line, with the date to ask.
Priya, on a student visa, has one. When a page wouldn't load, the agent said so, and asked her.
In the interview room, the agent plays a real professor, built from her public papers, and says it's practice. It scores each answer, and tells Priya to cut the line where she doubts herself.
Then it digs. Priya owns the gap and names the experiment she'd run. Depth goes from three to five.
At the writing desk, writer drafts a fit paragraph from her files, and critic marks the sentence a tired reader would stop at.
Every sentence carries a source. The checker fails a sentence without one, and any paper no tool returned. And no agent sends, submits or pays. People do.
Getting in is the start, not the finish. Offer room. Built with Switch.
